correctness.rationale: The six-class theorem is correct in the stated inclusion-only language. After choosing X and Y, the final choice Z can test the common cell X∩Y only for whether all of it lies in Z, and the cell outside X∪Y only for whether none of it lies in Z. Each of those two cells can therefore be capped at one for final-move types. The two cross cells need a cap of two, since their chosen and unchosen parts can affect different inclusions. When a first-move region has size at least three, its second-move split into a cap-two cell and a cap-one cell has the same four possible capped pairs (0,1), (1,1), (2,1), (2,0), independent of its size. Thus first-move types depend only on the two side sizes capped at three; all n≥6 attain the same pairs. For sharpness, relative to X, rank at most two expresses |X|≥1 by a strict predecessor, |X|≥2 by a two-step descending chain, and |X|≥3 by a Y strictly below X that has a strict predecessor and admits a strict intermediate element between Y and X. Dual formulas test |[n]\X|≥j for j≤3. Existentially quantifying X with both tests expresses n≥i+j for thresholds through six. An independent exact bounded replay also matched all 18 stated local comparisons and the finite equality pattern through n=7. No uploaded script was executed.
residual_risks: The independent replay is bounded and uses Venn cells, not literal subset enumeration; the analytic argument handles the infinite tail and sharpness.
